hints: Focus on where each dip appears on the wavenumber scale, since different bonds absorb in very characteristic regions.
Peak X is a sharp dip just below $3000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$, which is the classic region for $\text{C-H}$ stretching, not the broad band expected for $\text{O-H}$.
Peak Y is a very strong, sharp dip around $1700 \text{ cm}^{-1}$, so link that to the strong carbonyl absorption and check which formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$ isomer fits.
walkthrough:
**Read the spectrum axes**

Remember a dip (low transmittance) means strong absorption at that wavenumber. Here peak X is at about $2950 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ and peak Y is at about $1720 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

Rule to use:
$$\text{low transmittance = absorption by a bond vibration}$$

**Identify peak X around $3000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$**

This sharp absorption just below $3000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ is typical for $\text{C-H}$ stretching in alkanes, alkenes or aldehydes. An $\text{O-H}$ stretch would look very different, as a much broader dip centred around $3200$ to $3600 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

$$\text{C-H stretch} \approx 2850-3100 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ (sharp)}$$

**Identify peak Y around $1700 \text{ cm}^{-1}$**

This very strong, sharp dip is the textbook position for a carbonyl group. A $\text{C=C}$ stretch is much weaker and appears a little lower, around $1610$ to $1680 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

$$\text{C=O stretch} \approx 1680-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ (strong, sharp)}$$

**Link to the formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$**

The combination of $\text{C-H}$ plus $\text{C=O}$ fits ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, perfectly. So peak X is $\text{C-H}$ and peak Y is $\text{C=O}$.

options.A: Half right but half wrong. Peak X as $\text{C-H}$ is correct, but peak Y cannot be $\text{C=C}$ because the Y dip is too strong and at too high a wavenumber (about $1720 \text{ cm}^{-1}$). $\text{C=C}$ gives a weaker absorption around $1610$ to $1680 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.
options.B: Exactly right. Peak X near $2950 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ is the sharp $\text{C-H}$ stretch, and peak Y near $1720 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ is the strong sharp $\text{C=O}$ stretch of an aldehyde or ketone. This matches $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$ as ethanal.
options.C: Incorrect for both peaks. There is no broad $\text{O-H}$ band around $3200$ to $3600 \text{ cm}^{-1}$, so the substance is not an alcohol or acid. Peak Y is also too strong and too high for $\text{C=C}$.
options.D: Peak Y as $\text{C=O}$ is correct, but peak X cannot be $\text{O-H}$. Students sometimes confuse any peak near $3000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ with $\text{O-H}$, but $\text{O-H}$ is broad and centred higher, while X is sharp and just below $3000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$, characteristic of $\text{C-H}$.
